reply_text:
*I’d hold shipping for one high-priority bug.*

*P1 — Renewal dates use the wrong month’s length* — `src/schedule.js:6–7`
The day is clamped against the *source* month, then used to construct a date in the *next* month. JavaScript rolls invalid dates forward, so this can skip a renewal month or lose the anchor:

| From | Anchor | Expected | Actual |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Jan 31, 2026 | 31 | Feb 28 | Mar 3 |
| Jan 31, 2028 | 31 | Feb 29 | Mar 2 |
| Feb 28, 2026 | 31 | Mar 31 | Mar 28 |
| Apr 30, 2026 | 31 | May 31 | May 30 |

Repeated calls with anchor 31 produce `Jan 31 → Mar 3 → May 1 → Jul 1`, skipping entire billing months.

*Recommended fix:* clamp against the *target* month’s length, keeping the original anchor. Add regression tests for short-month entry, restoration after February, leap years, and consecutive renewals.

*Validation:* All 5 existing tests pass, but they miss these boundaries. A separate 2026–2029 matrix found 54 incorrect results across 1,488 cases.

Reviewed `billing-anniversary` at `f73b00d` against `main` at `7f89e48`. No files changed.
